questions.question: In Nomadic herding, herdsmen move from place to place with their animals for _______ and _______ along defined routes.

__
 
• Nomadic herding is practiced in the semi-arid and arid regions of **Sahara, Central Asia,** and some parts of India, like **Rajasthan and Jammu, and Kashmir**.

• This type of movement arises in response to climatic constraints and terrain.

questions.question: ______ is land which is left fallow (uncultivated) for more than five years and can be brought under cultivation after improving it through reclamation practices.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Culturable wasteland**__.

__
 
• **Culturable Waste-Land:** Any land which is left fallow (uncultivated) for **more than five years** is included in this category.

 
 
• It can be brought under cultivation after improving it through reclamation practices.
 
 
 
• If the land is left uncultivated for **more than five years**, it would be categorized as culturable wasteland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Permanent Pastures and Grazing Lands:** Most of this type of land is owned by the village** ‘Panchayat’ or the Government**. Only a small proportion of this land is **privately owned**.

 
 
• The land owned by the village panchayat comes under **‘Common Property Resources’**.
 
 
 
• **Current Fallow**:** **This is the land that is left without cultivation for one or less than one agricultural year.
 
 
• Fallowing is a cultural practice adopted for giving the land rest. The land** recoups lost fertility through natural processes**.

__
 
• The Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) is a **public sector undertaking (PSU)** in India.
 
• SAIL is one of the largest steel-making companies in India and one of the **Maharatnas of India's Central Public Sector Enterprises**.
 
• It was established in 1973 and operates under the **Ministry of Steel, Government of India**.
 
• SAIL owns and operates **five integrated steel plants** at Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur, Bokaro, and Burnpur (Asansol), and three special steel plants at Salem, Durgapur, and Bhadravati.

• **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)**

 
 
• PSUs are government-owned corporations or state-owned enterprises created by the government to undertake commercial activities on behalf of the government.
 
• These entities are either wholly or partially owned by the government and are typically involved in industries considered crucial for the country's economy.
 
 
 
• **Maharatna Status**
 
 
• This status is granted to select CPSEs to empower them to expand operations and emerge as global giants.
 
• Companies with Maharatna status have greater autonomy compared to other PSUs in terms of investment decisions, mergers, and acquisitions.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Steel**
 
 
• This is the apex body responsible for formulating policies and strategies for the growth of the steel industry in India.
 
• The ministry ensures coordination among various stakeholders, including public and private sector steel companies.

• These are large-scale industrial setups that carry out all processes from raw material processing to finished steel production.
 
• They include various stages such as coke production, sintering, iron making, steel making, and rolling.

questions.question: Unemployment is measured in India on the methods prescribed by the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__National Sample Survey Organisation.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Unemployment **is **measured in India** on the methods prescribed **by **the **National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO)**.

 
 
• According to the **International Labour Organization (ILO)**, **unemployment **is defined as** not having a job but is available for work and actively looking for one.**
 
• The **unemployment rate** is measured as the **ratio of the unemployed to the labour force.**
 
• The total number of employed and unemployed people is known as the** labor force.**
 
 
• People who are neither employed nor jobless, such as students and people who perform unpaid household labor, are seen as not being in the labor force.
 
 
 
 
 
• The **NSSO **is the nodal agency responsible for **conducting surveys and collecting data on various socio-economic aspects** of the country, including employment and unemployment.
 
 
• It was **set up in 1950** to conduct periodic surveys on employment and unemployment, which are used to estimate the unemployment rate in the country.
 
• In **2019**, the Central Statistical Office (**CSO**) and the National Sample Survey Office (**NSSO**) **combined **to **become **the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MOSPI).**
 
 
 
• Apart from NSSO, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also publishes data on employment and unemployment, but it is primarily focused on the banking and financial sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **National Employment Department** under **Ministry of Labour & Employment** is responsible for formulating policies and schemes for employment generation and skill development in the country.
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is India’s central bank.
 
 
• In compliance with the terms of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934,** it was **founded **on **April 1, 1935** in **Calcutta**.
 
 
• It was permanently** moved to Mumbai in 1937.**
 
 
 
• Though originally privately owned, since **nationalisation in 1949**, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India.
 
• It regulates the** issue of Bank notes** and **keeping of reserves** with a view to securing** monetary stability in India **and generally to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• It also monitors the monetary policies through its **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).**
 
 
 
• The **National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE)** was **founded **in **1992 **with the main goal of** increasing market transparency in India's equity markets.**
 
 
• It was **recognised **as a stock exchange** by SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) in1993** and started its **operations in 1994.**
 
• Its **headquarters is in Mumbai.** It is a market facilitator for trades in wholesale debt, stocks, and derivatives.
 
• In **1994**, it **became the first exchange in India to provide modern, completely automated electronic trading.**

questions.question: __________ represents a potential for further intellectual growth and contribution to economic-socio-cultural development of society.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Literacy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Literacy enables individuals to acquire knowledge and develop critical thinking skills, which are essential for personal and societal growth.
 
• High literacy rates are often correlated with economic development and social progress, as literate populations are better equipped to participate in the economy and contribute to social and cultural advancements.
 
• Literacy is a fundamental human right and a cornerstone for achieving other rights, empowering individuals to improve their living standards and participate fully in community and national affairs.
 
• Promoting literacy can help reduce poverty and inequality by providing people with the skills needed to access better employment opportunities and improve their quality of life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census**

 
 
• A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.
 
• It is conducted periodically by governments to collect data on the population's size, distribution, and various demographic characteristics.
 
• This data is crucial for planning and delivering public services, such as healthcare, education, and infrastructure.
 
• In many countries, censuses are conducted every ten years.
 
 
 
• **Economy**
 
 
• The economy refers to the system of production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services within a society or geographic area.
 
• It encompasses various sectors, including agriculture, industry, and services, and is influenced by factors such as government policies, market conditions, and global trends.
 
• Economic growth is often measured by indicators such as Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and employment rates.
 
• Economic stability and growth are essential for improving living standards and reducing poverty.
 
 
 
• **Politics**
 
 
• Politics involves the activities associated with governance, including the formulation and implementation of policies, laws, and regulations.
 
• It encompasses various institutions and processes, such as elections, political parties, and government agencies.
 
• Political systems can vary widely, from democracies to authoritarian regimes, each with different approaches to governance and citizen participation.
 
• Effective political governance is crucial for maintaining social order, protecting citizens' rights, and promoting economic and social development.

questions.question: Which coal is low-grade, brown and soft with high moisture content?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lignite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lignite is a type of coal that is considered to be low-grade due to its relatively low energy content.
 
• It is brown in color and has a soft texture, making it easier to break apart compared to harder forms of coal.
 
• Lignite has a high moisture content, sometimes as much as 45-66%, which reduces its efficiency as a fuel source.
 
• Despite its lower quality, lignite is often used in electricity generation, particularly in power plants located near lignite mines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metallurgical Coal**

 
 
• Also known as coking coal, it is primarily used in steel production.
 
• It has a high carbon content and low impurities, which are essential for producing high-quality coke.
 
• Metallurgical coal undergoes a coking process where it is heated in the absence of air to remove volatile substances, leaving behind a solid carbon mass called coke.
 
 
 
• **Bituminous Coal**
 
 
• It is a middle-rank coal between sub-bituminous and anthracite.
 
• Bituminous coal is used extensively for electricity generation and as a fuel in industries.
 
• It has a higher carbon content than lignite and sub-bituminous coal, providing more energy when burned.
 
 
 
• **Anthracite**
 
 
• It is the highest rank of coal due to its high carbon content and low impurities.
 
• Anthracite is hard, shiny, and has the highest energy content of all coal types.
 
• It is used for heating residential and commercial buildings and in some industrial processes.

questions.question: In migration the factors which cause people to leave their place of residence or origin are called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Push factors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Push factors are the factors that cause individuals or groups to leave their place of residence or origin and move to a new location.**
 
• Push factors are negative or unfavorable circumstances that make people want to leave their homes or countries. These factors could be related to economic, social, political, or environmental conditions.
 
• Examples of push factors include poverty, unemployment, lack of opportunities, political instability, war, natural disasters, and environmental degradation. These factors make people feel like they have no choice but to leave their homes and seek a better life elsewhere.
 
• Push factors are different from pull factors, which are positive or attractive conditions that encourage people to move to a new location. Pull factors could include better job opportunities, higher wages, better living conditions, or a safer environment.
 
• Understanding push and pull factors is important for policymakers and researchers who want to understand migration patterns and develop effective policies to address the root causes of migration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Pull factors: **As mentioned earlier, pull factors are positive or attractive conditions that encourage people to move to a new location. Pull factors are the opposite of push factors and could include better job opportunities, higher wages, better living conditions, or a safer environment.
 
• **Regular factors: **This option is not related to the question and does not make sense in the context of migration. Regular factors could refer to factors that occur regularly or frequently, but it is not clear how this would relate to migration.
 
• **Irregular factors:** This option is also not related to the question and does not make sense in the context of migration. Irregular factors could refer to factors that are unusual or irregular, but it is not clear how this would relate to migration.

questions.question: A settlement in closely built area of dwellings, wherever flat land is available is called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Compact settlement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A settlement in closely built area of dwellings, wherever flat land is available is called **Compact settlement**.
 
• These settlements **develop generally in the fertile plains** and **valleys**.
 
• The **density **of population is **high **due to productive land.
 
• **Agriculture** is the **main occupation** of the people.
 
• These have **problems** **of sanitation** and **drainage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In urban planning, the **grid plan**, **grid street plan**, or **gridiron plan** is a type of city plan in which **streets run at right angles** to each other, forming a grid.
 
• A **Line settlement **or **Linear settlement **is a collection of buildings or a settlement that is created in a long line; these are often modest to medium-sized settlements.
 
 
• A lot of these **communities are built along transportation corridors** like **roads**, **rivers**, or **canals**.
 
• Others arise as a result of geographical limitations like hills, valleys, mountains, and coasts. A linear colony might not have a clear center.
 
 
 
• One of the primary categories of settlement patterns that landscape historians use to categorize rural communities in England and other countries is the **dispersed settlement**, also referred to as the **scattered settlement.**
 
 
• Usually, the region is made up of several distinct farmsteads dispersed all across it.
 
• Houses in dispersed villages are few and spaced widely apart.
 
• These kinds of villages are typically found in **high terrain regions**, **hot deserts**, grasslands, deep forests, and vast agricultural fields.

questions.question: The __________ results from an increase in the proportion of workers relative to nonworkers in the population.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**demographic dividend**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **demographic dividend** refers to the economic growth potential that can result from shifts in a population’s age structure.
 
• This shift occurs when the proportion of the working-age population (15-64 years) is larger compared to the non-working-age population (below 15 and above 64 years).
 
• During this period, the workforce grows more rapidly than the dependent population, providing a window of opportunity for economic growth.
 
• To harness the demographic dividend, it is crucial to invest in health, education, and employment opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of the demographic dividend is closely linked to the demographic transition theory, which describes the transition from high birth and death rates to lower birth and death rates as a country develops.
 
• Countries in different stages of this transition can experience varying economic impacts based on their demographic profiles.
 
• Effective policy measures and investments in human capital are essential to convert the demographic potential into actual economic benefits.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a ‘Navratna’ or ‘Maharatna’ company in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Industrial Finance Corporation of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) is not classified as either a 'Navratna' or 'Maharatna' company in India.
 
• IFCI is a development finance institution in India, established to provide long-term financial assistance to the industrial sector.
 
• The company was established in 1948 as a statutory corporation and was later converted into a company under the Companies Act, 1956.
 
• Unlike 'Navratna' or 'Maharatna' companies, which are typically large and profitable public sector enterprises, IFCI focuses on providing financial support for industrial development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Navratna Companies:**

 
 
• Navratna is a status given to certain public sector enterprises (PSEs) in India that have comparative advantages and greater autonomy to compete in the global market.
 
• To be eligible for Navratna status, a company must have achieved a certain level of financial performance and operational efficiency.
 
• Navratna companies enjoy greater financial and operational autonomy compared to other PSEs.
 
• Examples of Navratna companies include Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), and National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO).
 
 
 
• **Maharatna Companies:**
 
 
• Maharatna is a status given to the largest and most profitable public sector enterprises in India.
 
• To qualify for Maharatna status, a company must have a substantial global presence and significant operational and financial autonomy.
 
• Maharatna companies have greater flexibility in investment and expansion decisions.
 
• Examples of Maharatna companies include Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Oil & Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), and National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC).
 
 
 
• **Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI):**
 
 
• IFCI was established in 1948 to provide long-term financial assistance to the industrial sector in India.
 
• It was the first Development Financial Institution (DFI) in the country.
 
• IFCI's main objective is to provide financial support for the growth and development of industries in India.
 
• It offers a range of financial products and services, including project finance, corporate loans, and advisory services.
 
 
 
• **Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs):**
 
 
• PSEs are government-owned corporations or companies in which the central or state government holds a majority stake.
 
• They play a crucial role in the economic development of the country by providing essential services and infrastructure.
 
• PSEs are categorized into different statuses such as Miniratna, Navratna, and Maharatna based on their performance and strategic importance.
 
• The government provides different levels of autonomy and financial powers to these enterprises based on their status.

questions.question: Among the following industries, the promotion of one industry is part of the directive principle of state policy of our Constitution and that industry is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cottage industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Constitution of India under the Directive Principles of State Policy includes the **promotion of cottage industries in rural areas** as one of its goals (Article 43).
 
• Cottage industries play a crucial role in the **economic development of rural areas** by providing employment and supporting the traditional economy.
 
• These industries are typically **small-scale operations** run by families using their own equipment and resources.
 
• The **promotion of cottage industries** helps in preserving traditional crafts and skills, which are an integral part of India's cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**

 
 
• These are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in consideration while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are contained in Part IV of the Constitution of India, covering Articles 36 to 51.
 
• These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They also aim to establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state.
 
 
 
• **Cottage Industry**
 
 
• It refers to small-scale production activities typically carried out at home by family members using their own equipment.
 
• These industries are labor-intensive and rely heavily on traditional skills and methods.
 
• Cottage industries are crucial for the economic development of rural areas as they provide employment and help in the utilization of local resources.
 
• Examples include handloom weaving, pottery, handicrafts, and embroidery.
 
 
 
• **Economic Development in Rural Areas**
 
 
• It involves improving the quality of life and economic well-being of people living in relatively isolated and sparsely populated areas.
 
• Promotion of rural industries, including cottage industries, is an essential part of rural economic development.
 
• It helps in reducing migration to urban areas by providing local employment opportunities.
 
• Rural development initiatives often include improving infrastructure, education, and healthcare alongside promoting industries.

questions.question: In which state is the Jhumming cultivation known as Dahiya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jhumming cultivation is a traditional form of shifting agriculture practiced in various states of India.
 
• In Madhya Pradesh, this form of agriculture is specifically known as Dahiya.
 
• It involves clearing a piece of land by cutting down and burning vegetation, then cultivating crops on it for a few years before moving to a new area.
 
• Dahiya is practiced mainly by the tribal communities in the hilly regions of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• This method is part of the cultural heritage and agricultural practices of these tribal communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shifting Cultivation**

 
 
• It is an agricultural system in which plots of land are cultivated temporarily, then abandoned and allowed to revert to their natural vegetation.
 
• This cycle is repeated as the farmer moves to a new area.
 
• Shifting cultivation is also known as slash-and-burn agriculture.
 
• It is commonly practiced in tropical rainforests and hilly terrains.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**
 
 
• Shifting cultivation can lead to deforestation and loss of biodiversity if not managed sustainably.
 
• It can also cause soil erosion and degradation over time.
 
• Sustainable practices are necessary to mitigate these environmental impacts.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Communities**
 
 
• Tribal communities in India often rely on traditional agricultural practices like shifting cultivation.
 
• These practices are deeply rooted in their cultural and social systems.
 
• Government policies and programs aim to support sustainable agricultural practices among tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Policies**
 
 
• The Indian government has various schemes to promote sustainable agriculture and support farmers.
 
• Programs focus on improving agricultural productivity, sustainability, and farmers' livelihoods.
 
• Efforts include providing training, financial assistance, and access to modern agricultural technologies.

questions.question: As per census 2011, what is the Total Fertility Rate in India? (provide an approximate range)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.1 - 2.9**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Total Fertility Rate:-**

 
 
• 
 
**It is a demographic indicator that measures the average number of children a woman would have during her reproductive years, usually between the ages of 15 and 49, if she were to experience the age-specific fertility rates observed in a specific population during a specific period.**

 
 
• 
 
TFR is calculated by summing up the age-specific fertility rates (the number of live births to women in specific age groups) and is often expressed as the number of children per woman or per 1,000 women. It is a crucial measure for understanding population dynamics and growth.

 
 
• 
 
A TFR of around 2.1 is considered the "replacement level" fertility rate, meaning that, on average, each woman is having enough children to replace herself and her partner in the population. If the TFR is below 2.1, the population may experience a decline in the long term, while a TFR above 2.1 would result in population growth.

 
 
• 
 
**As per the 2011 census, the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) in India was approximately 2.1 to 2.9.**

questions.question: What do you call the maximum sustainable size of a resident population in a given ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Carrying capacity__.**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The maximum sustainable size of a resident population in a given ecosystem is called as Carrying capacity.**
 
• Carrying capacity is the** maximum number, density, or biomass of a population that a specific area can support sustainably.**
 
• This likely varies over time and depends on environmental factors, resources, and the presence of predators, disease agents, and competitors over time.
 
• The concept of carrying capacity has been explicitly recognized for more than 175 years, and its use has waxed and waned during this time.
 
• Currently, the use of carrying capacity to describe any particular population requires caution, although the concept remains intuitive and invokes questions that challenge our fundamental understanding of factors that regulate populations over time and space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**Census**__

__
 
• An official, usually periodic enumeration of a population, often including the collection of related **demographic information**.
 
• Demography Economic Activity Literacy and Education Housing & Household Amenities Urbanization, Fertility, and Mortality Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Language are some of the information that we can get from census data.

**Crude rate**__

 
• **A crude rate** is defined as the total number of events, or count, divided by the **mid-year total population of the selected geography and multiplied by a constant, which is a multiple of 10.**
 
• Typical constants used for public health rates include 100, 1,000, 10,000, or 100,000.
 
• Crude Rate = **(Number of Events or Count ÷ Mid-year Population) x Constant**.
 
• Crude rates are the only types of rates available in the Birth MICA, Pregnancy MICA, Fertility and Pregnancy Rate MICA, and the five WIC MICAs.
 
• Crude rates are reported in the Community Data Profiles for birth, pregnancy, and WIC indicators. 
 
• Rates for specific age groups, such as infants under the age of **1 or** **adults ages 20-24**, are also crude rates unless otherwise specified. (Age groups that cover a large range of ages, such as adults** ages 18-64**, maybe age-adjusted.)

questions.question: How many industries have been reserved for the public sector under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 categorized industries into three schedules.
 
• Schedule A listed 17 industries exclusively reserved for the public sector.
 
• These industries were considered crucial for the nation's economy and included arms and ammunition, atomic energy, railways, etc.
 
• The objective was to ensure state control over the commanding heights of the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956:**

 
 
• This policy aimed at accelerating the rate of economic growth and speeding up industrialization.
 
• It emphasized the role of the state in the development of industries and the importance of the public sector in commanding heights of the economy.
 
• The resolution classified industries into three categories – Schedule A, Schedule B, and Schedule C.
 
• Schedule A contained 17 industries exclusively reserved for the public sector, Schedule B included industries where both the public and private sectors could operate, and Schedule C was open to the private sector with state intervention as needed.
 
 
 
• **Public Sector:**
 
 
• The portion of an economy composed of all levels of government and government-controlled enterprises.
 
• Public sector industries are typically those that are considered vital for national interests and include sectors like defense, energy, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Schedule A Industries:**
 
 
• These included industries of strategic importance like arms and ammunition, atomic energy, railways, air transport, and defense equipment.
 
• The government aimed to have complete control and ownership over these industries to ensure national security and self-reliance.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956:**
 
 
• To establish a socialistic pattern of society by expanding the public sector.
 
• To reduce income and wealth inequalities.
 
• To prevent the concentration of economic power in few hands.
 
• To promote balanced regional development by setting up industries in backward areas.

• **A site is described as a location where something is built**, or constructed, or as a location where a major or historical event took place.
 
• A site would be the property you purchase and plan to build your new home on.
 
• **The physical qualities of the local terrain are included in the term "site," which refers to the actual location of a colony on Earth. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Settlements**

 
 
• Humans who have established a stable community over an extended period of time in a particular location are considered to **live in settlements**.
 
• A modest fishing town on a river in a distant place can be considered a settlement, as opposed to a metropolis, which is a **sophisticated population hub**.
 
• **Towns, villages, cities, hamlets, bases**, and** camps** are some of the several names for settlements.
 
• Any planned pattern of human living can be categorized as a **settlement**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about migration in India?

options.text: Migration may be rural to urban.

• **Migration in India** refers to the movement of people from one place to another within the country's borders.
 
• This movement can be temporary or permanent and can occur due to various factors such as **economic, social, political, or environmental reasons.**
 
• Migration in India has been a significant phenomenon throughout its history and continues to shape the country's demographic, social, and economic landscape.

• Migration patterns in India are influenced by various factors, including economic disparities between regions, uneven development, demographic changes, social networks, government policies, and environmental factors such as droughts, floods, or natural disasters.
 
• While migration can bring opportunities for individuals and contribute to economic growth and cultural diversity, it also presents challenges, such as urban overcrowding, strain on infrastructure and services, social tensions, and exploitation of migrant workers.

questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, which of the following groups of union territories has the highest literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshadweep and Daman & Diu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census of India 2011**, among UTs (Union Territories), **Lakshadweep **has maximum** ****91.85%** of literacy rate and **Daman & Diu** comes next with **87.10%**.
 
• The literacy rate (in % of age of population) of other UTs are: **Andaman & Nicobar - 86.63**, **Delhi - 86.21**, **Chandigarh - 86.05**, **Puducherry - 85.85**, **Dadra and Nagar Haveli - 76.34**.
 
• Among states, the highest literacy rate, as per the 2011 Census, is in Kerala with 94%.
 
 
• The least literate state is Bihar, with 61.80% literacy, Maharashtra has 82.34% and Tamil Nadu has 80.09% literacy.
 
• The overall literacy rate in India is 74%.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Census of India 2011:

 
 
• It started on April 1, 2010.
 
• "Our Census, Our Future" was the 2011 census's slogan.
 
• India's population, according to the 2011 Census, is estimated to be 1.21 billion.
 
• The population density was 382 persons per square kilometer in 2011.
 
• India's sex ratio, as per the 2011 census, is 940.
 
• India's child sex ratio is 918, the lowest since the country's independence, as per Census 2011.
 
• This marked the commencement of the 15th Census of India and the 7th Census of Independent India (2011).
 
• The Indian Census Commissioner for 2011 was C. Chandramouli.
 
• The 2011 India Census was carried out in two phases:
 
 
• House listing and Housing Census (April to September 2010).
 
• Population Enumeration (9th to 28 February 2011).
 
 
 
 
 
• The 1948 Census Act governs how the census is carried out.
 
 
• The Indian Home Minister at the time, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, spearheaded the bill for this Act.
 
• The Indian Constitution's Article 246 declares the population census to be a Union subject.
 
• It is mentioned in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution under serial number 69.
 
• The Ministry of Home Affairs' Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner oversees the decennial census.
 
 
 
• The first census of India was conducted by Lord Mayo in 1872.
 
• The first official census was started by Lord Ripon in 1881.
